verses.72:1: Como Deus é bom para Israel, * para os que são retos de coração!
verses.72:2: Mas os meus pés quase {moti}: * quase {effusi} os meus passos.
verses.72:3: Porque {zelavi} iníquos, * vendo a paz dos pecadores.
verses.72:4: Porque não há {respectus} morte deles: * e {firmamentum} no flagelo deles.
verses.72:5: Não estão na fadiga dos homens, * e com os homens não serão flagelados:
verses.72:6: Por isso a soberba os {tenuit}, * {operti} da sua iniquidade e impiedade.
verses.72:7: A iniquidade deles saiu como que da gordura: * passaram {affectus} do coração.
verses.72:8: Pensaram e falaram maldade: * falaram iniquidade {excelso8}.
verses.72:9: Puseram {incaelum} a sua boca: * e a língua deles passou pela terra.
verses.72:10: Por isso o meu povo se voltará {hic}: * e dias cheios serão achados neles.
verses.72:11: E disseram: Como é que Deus sabe, * e se há saber {excelso11}?
verses.72:13: E eu disse: Então sem causa {justificavi} o meu coração, * e lavei as minhas mãos entre os inocentes:
verses.72:14: E fui flagelado o dia todo, * {matutinis}.
verses.72:15: Se eu dizia: Narrarei assim: * eis que {reprobavi} a {natio} dos vossos filhos.
verses.72:16: Eu {existimabam} conhecer isto, * é fadiga diante de mim:
verses.72:17: Até que eu entre no santuário de Deus: * e entenda {novissimis}.
verses.72:19: {facti19}! De repente {defecerunt}: * pereceram por causa da sua iniquidade.
verses.72:20: Como o sonho dos que {surgentium}, Senhor, * na vossa cidade reduzireis a nada a imagem deles.
verses.72:21: Porque o meu coração se inflamou, e os meus rins {commutati}: * e eu fui reduzido a nada, e não soube.
verses.72:24: {tenuisti} a minha mão direita: e {voluntate} me guiastes, * e com glória me {suscepisti}.
verses.72:25: Pois o que há para mim no céu? * e que quis eu {ate} sobre a terra?
verses.72:26: {defecit} a minha carne e o meu coração: * Deus do meu coração, e {deus26} para sempre.
verses.72:27: Porque eis que os que {elongant} perecerão: * fizestes perecer todos os que {fornicantur}.
verses.72:28: Mas para mim é bom {adhaerere} a Deus: * pôr no Senhor Deus a minha esperança:
verses.72:28b: Para que eu anuncie {praedicationes}, * às portas da filha de Sião.

decisions.why: The *movéri* row (open) gives *ser abalado*, heard as shaken first and as falling second — the Latin's range (ἐσαλεύθησαν, 'were shaken'). 93:18 *Motus est pes meus* is the other place with feet. The passive is kept; *vacilar* is the row's option and MS1932's word, and it says the stumble more plainly but gives the verb an active, inner sense the passive does not have.

options.label: foram abalados
options.note: Ruling; the row's verb, the passive kept.

options.label: vacilaram
options.note: MS1932 *por pouco não vacilaram*; the row's option.

decisions.why: *effúndere* is poured out (ἐξεχύθη, the same Greek verb): the steps run away like spilt water. That is the image, and D42 gives *effúndere* the verb *derramar*. DRB *had well nigh slipped* and MS1932 *se transviaram* explain it into a stumble. Kept, as a concrete image (rule 5), and the ambiguity reader should test whether it is heard at all.

options.label: se derramaram
options.note: Ruling; the Latin's image and the effúndere verb.

options.label: escorregaram
options.note: DRB *slipped*; the sense, not the image.

decisions.why: The *zeláre* row (open, from Ps 36:1) says 72:3 should follow with *invejei*: ζηλόω of the wicked is envy (MS1932 *tive inveja dos iníquos*; DRB *I had a zeal on occasion of the wicked*). *ter zelo por* says the opposite in Portuguese, *ter ciúme de* is a lover's jealousy. *super* ('over, on account of') is absorbed by the transitive verb.

decisions.latin: Quia non est respéctus morti eórum
decisions.why: A crux. *respéctus* is a looking back, regard, consideration (L&S); the Greek ἀνάνευσις is a refusal or turning back. DRB *there is no regard to their death*; MS1932 paraphrases (*eles não têm medo da morte*). The Latin leaves open whose regard is missing (theirs for death, or anyone's for their death). *respeito a* is the Latin's word and 'regard to' in plain Portuguese, and leaves the owner open; *consideração* is the same sense, three syllables longer.

options.label: consideração pela
options.note: the same sense, plainer to some ears; +3 syllables.

options.label: temor da
options.note: MS1932's sense (*não têm medo da morte*); interprets.

decisions.why: D31 left 72:4 to be decided here. *firmaméntum* is said of the wicked, not of God and not of the sky: στερέωμα, 'firmness, strength' — DRB *strength in their stripes*. *esteio* (D31, God as prop) would make the stripes a prop; *firmamento* is only the sky in Portuguese. *firmeza* is the plain word of the sense. The second colon is verbless, as the Latin: whether the first colon's *non est* carries over (DRB *nor is there*) or not is left open (v1 supplied *há*; the latinist ruled that a major, v2 drops it). *plaga* (μάστιγι) → *flagelo* by D39. *deles* twice, as *eórum* twice.

options.label: esteio
options.note: D31's word for God as support.

options.label: firmamento
options.note: the cognate; heard as the sky.

options.label: e há firmeza
options.note: draft 1; supplies a positive verb and settles the ellipsis.

decisions.latin: ténuit eos supérbia … Tenuísti manum déxteram meam
decisions.why: The Latin has one verb (and the Greek one, ἐκράτησεν / ἐκράτησας) for pride seizing the wicked and God holding the psalmist's right hand: the psalm turns on it. One Portuguese verb keeps the turn. *tomar* serves both: *a soberba os tomou* (as fear 'takes' a man) and *Tomastes a minha mão direita* (MS1932 *Tomaste-me pela minha mão direita*). *segurar* is the verb to the letter but *a soberba os segurou* is weak; *prender* is DRB's *held them fast* and hostile at 72:24.

options.label: prender / tomar
options.note: DRB 'held them fast' at 72:6; loses the echo.

decisions.latin: opérti sunt iniquitáte et impietáte sua
decisions.why: Latin passive (*opérti sunt*), Greek middle (περιεβάλοντο, 'they wrapped themselves'). The passive is kept; *cobertos de* is natural Portuguese. MS1932 *estão cobertos* makes it a present state.

options.label: foram cobertos
options.note: Ruling; the Latin's voice and tense.

decisions.why: διῆλθον εἰς διάθεσιν καρδίας, 'they passed into the disposition of the heart': they went over to what the heart craved. DRB *the affection of the heart*; MS1932 *abandonaram-se às paixões do seu coração* (another verb). The singular *afeto* is heard in Brazil as fondness; the plural *afetos* keeps its older sense, the movements of the heart (the ascetic writers' *afetos desordenados*) — the number is grammar (D2). *transíre* → *passar*, as in 72:9.

options.label: aos afetos
options.note: Ruling; the cognate in the plural.

options.label: ao afeto
options.note: the Latin's number; heard as fondness.

decisions.latin: iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt … et si est sciéntia in excélso?
decisions.why: The same Latin phrase twice, four verses apart (the Greek differs: εἰς τὸ ὕψος, then ἐν τῷ ὑψίστῳ, 'in the Most High'). The Latin's repetition is kept with one wording. *no alto* is the plain local phrase and holds both: the wicked talk loftily / up at heaven, and they ask whether there is knowledge up there. MS1932 *altivamente* at 72:8 explains and cannot serve 72:11; *no Altíssimo* at 72:11 is the Greek, not the Latin.

options.label: no alto
options.note: Ruling; one wording for the one phrase.

options.label: nas alturas
options.note: the excélsa row's noun; the Latin is a singular.

options.label: com altivez / no alto
options.note: MS1932's manner at 72:8; breaks the repetition.

decisions.why: *in* + accusative: into, towards, against. DRB and MS1932 both read *against heaven*; the Greek εἰς οὐρανόν is as open as the Latin. *no céu* keeps the Latin's openness (their mouth set up in heaven, speaking as if from there — which the second colon answers: *and their tongue went through the earth*). *contra* decides for hostility.

*hic* is 'here' (ἐνταῦθα). *se voltará* keeps the medio-passive and the *convértere → voltar* row; bare *voltará* would be heard as 'come back' (the risk D44 records at 54:4). Brazilian says 'turn here' as *para cá*; *para aqui* is European. MS1932's gloss explains: his people will turn to the side of the wicked.

options.label: para cá
options.note: Ruling; the Brazilian adverb of place.

options.label: para aqui
options.note: the adverb to the letter; European.

decisions.latin: Ecce, ipsi peccatóres, et abundántes in sǽculo, * obtinuérunt divítias
decisions.why: Three choices in one colon. (1) *Ecce, ipsi peccatóres* has no verb; DRB reads a predicate (*Behold these are sinners*). Draft 1 followed it; v2 keeps the Latin's single clause, *ipsi peccatóres et abundántes* in apposition to the subject of *obtinuérunt*. (2) *abundántes* (εὐθηνοῦντες, 'prospering'): *abundantes* said of persons is heard in Brazil as 'numerous', a wrong first hearing, so *prósperos*; the *abundántia* row keeps *abundância* for the noun and names *prosperidade* as its option. (3) *in sǽculo* (ablative; the Greek has εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα) is 'in the world, in this age': *no mundo* (DRB *in the world*, MS1932 *neste mundo*). D30 gives *mundo* to *orbis terræ*; the two never meet in this psalm.

options.label: eles mesmos, pecadores e prósperos no mundo

forms.ecce12: Eis que eles mesmos, pecadores e

options.note: Ruling (v2); *ipsi* → *eles mesmos*, the apposition kept, as the latinist and the stylist asked.

options.label: os próprios pecadores … abundantes no mundo

forms.ecce12: Eis que os próprios pecadores, e

options.note: the Latin to the letter, *ipsi* as the subject; *abundantes* heard as 'many'.

options.label: … prósperos neste século

forms.ecce12: Eis que estes são pecadores, e

options.note: *sǽculum* as the age; *século* in this sense is bookish.

options.label: estes são pecadores … prósperos no mundo

forms.ecce12: Eis que estes são pecadores, e,

options.note: draft 1; DRB's parse with a supplied verb.

decisions.latin: Ergo sine causa justificávi cor meum
decisions.why: ἐδικαίωσα τὴν καρδίαν, 'I made my heart just / kept it righteous'. The cognate *justifiquei* is the Latin's word and the theological one, but a Brazilian first hears 'I made excuses for'. MS1932 *purifiquei* is another word (*mundáre*). Kept, as a word Catholics also know in its sense of 'make just'; the ambiguity reader should test it. The ambiguity reader heard *justifiquei* as 'I excused myself', the wrong first hearing; v2 takes *tornei justo*.

options.label: tornei justo
options.note: Ruling (v2); the sense, which the cognate hid.

options.label: justifiquei
options.note: draft 1; the Latin's word, heard as 'I made excuses for'.

decisions.why: The *matutína* row (open, Ps 62:7) says 72:14 should follow: *nas madrugadas*, the plural kept apart from *mane → de manhã* (the Greek εἰς τὰς πρωίας). The colon is verbless in Latin and stays so; the comma lets it be heard as 'and my chastisement [was there] at the dawns'. *castigátio* is the noun of *castigáre* (→ *castigar*); the Greek is ἔλεγχος (reproof), which by D39 would be *repreensão* — the Latin's word is followed.

options.label: e o meu castigo, nas madrugadas

forms.matutinis: e o meu castigo, nas madrugadas
e o meu castigo vinha nas madrugadas
e o meu castigo, pelas manhãs

decisions.why: The Latin is an indicative perfect after an imperfect condition: 'if I said … behold, I [have] rejected the race of your sons' — the Greek ἠσυνθέτηκα is 'I have broken faith with'. DRB (*I should condemn*) and MS1932 (*via que condenava*) turn it into a conditional or add a verb. *reprobáre → rejeitar* is the glossary's (117:22). The indicative is kept; the sense (to speak as the wicked do would be to disown God's children) is left to the hearer, as the Latin leaves it. *nátio*: *nação* (MS1932) is the Latin's word; *geração* (the Greek γενεά, DRB) would collide with *generátio / progénies*, and *nações* is already the word for *gentes* — they do not meet in this psalm.

decisions.latin: Existimábam ut cognóscerem hoc, * labor est ante me
decisions.why: ὑπέλαβον τοῦ γνῶναι τοῦτο, 'I took it up, so as to know this'. *existimáre → pensar* (D44). *pensava em conhecer* is how Portuguese says turning the mind towards knowing; *pensava, para conhecer* keeps the purpose clause to the letter but is stiff. MS1932 *Reflecti para compreender isto* (other verbs). The second colon keeps the Latin's present and its verbless subject (*labor est* → *é uma fadiga*), *labor → fadiga* by the row.

εἰς τὰ ἔσχατα αὐτῶν, 'their last things, their end'. DRB *their last ends*, MS1932 *qual será o fim deles*. *o fim deles* says it plainly and loses the plural and the *in*; *as últimas coisas deles* keeps both and is flat; *os novíssimos* is the catechism's word for the last things, unknown to most. Present subjunctives (*intrem … intéllegam*) kept: *até que eu entre … e entenda*.

*posuísti* has no object in Latin or Greek (ἔθου αὐτοῖς). DRB supplies *it* (*thou hast put it to them*); MS1932 supplies a whole noun (*uma prosperidade enganosa*). Draft 1 supplied a neuter *o*; the stylist and the ambiguity reader found the ear searching for its antecedent, and the latinist asked for no object. Brazilian Portuguese leaves the object of *pôr* unspoken in speech, so v2 follows the Latin; what was set (their prosperity, a snare, a punishment) stays open. *propter dolos* → *por causa dos enganos*, the *dolus* row; whose deceits is open, as in the Latin. *Verúmtamen → Todavia*, the row.

options.label: pusestes para eles
options.note: Ruling (v2); objectless, as the Latin (Brazilian speech drops the object pronoun freely).

options.label: vós o pusestes para eles
options.note: draft 1; DRB's *it*, which the ear could not place.

forms.posuisti: vós lhes destes uma prosperidade enganosa

decisions.why: *allevaréntur* is passive, 'while they were being lifted up' (ἐν τῷ ἐπαρθῆναι): the Latin does not say who lifts them — themselves in pride, or God, who raised them and then threw them down. The passive keeps that open; MS1932 *se elevavam* decides for their pride.

options.label: vós os derrubastes enquanto eram elevados

forms.allev: vós os derrubastes enquanto eram elevados

options.note: Ruling (v2); the passive, the pronoun before the verb (stylist).

options.label: vós os derrubastes enquanto se elevavam

forms.allev: vós os derrubastes enquanto se elevavam

decisions.why: 'How they became a desolation' (ἐγένοντο εἰς ἐρήμωσιν). *se tornaram desolação* is *fíeri in* in plain Portuguese; the exclamation mark keeps *Como* from being heard as 'as' (a comparison or a time clause). MS1932 *foram reduzidos a uma tal desolação* borrows *reduzir*, which this psalm needs for *redígere* (72:20, 72:21).

options.label: Como se tornaram uma desolação
options.note: Ruling (v2); the article, as the stylist asked.

decisions.latin: súbito defecérunt … Defécit caro mea, et cor meum
decisions.why: One verb twice in the psalm, for the wicked who give out and for the psalmist's flesh and heart. The *defícere* row keeps *desfalecer* where things are the subject (72:26 is named there) and warns that with persons meaning 'be gone' it failed (11:2). At 72:19 the sense is 'gave out, came to an end' (ἐξέλιπον), as at 17:38 *até que desfaleçam*, which held. One verb keeps the echo between the end of the wicked and the psalmist's own failing, which the psalm means. *súbito → de repente*, the row (72:19 named).

*surgéntium*, 'of those rising' — from sleep (the Greek ἐξεγειρομένου, 'one awaking'; DRB and MS1932 *that awake / que despertam*). The Latin's verb is the plain one of getting up, and next to *sonho* it is heard as waking; *surgere / exsúrgere → levantar-se* in the glossary. *despertar* is another verb (*evigiláre*).

ἠλλοιώθησαν, 'were altered'. *renes → rins* (row; the organ named). The passive is kept; *se mudaram* would be heard as 'moved house', *se alteraram* as 'got upset'. MS1932 paraphrases (*as minhas entranhas se comoveram*).

options.label: se alteraram
options.note: the Greek's verb; heard as upset.

decisions.latin: Ut juméntum factus sum apud te
decisions.why: The *juménta* row gives *animais* for the plural (κτήνη), and asks whether the singular here is *animal*. The Greek is an adjective, κτηνώδης, 'beast-like, brutish'; *como um animal* says that in Brazil too (dull, without understanding, after 72:21 *e não soube*). *jumento* is the Latin's word to the letter but is a donkey in Brazil; MS1932 *animal de carga* adds the burden. *apud te → junto de vós*, the row (open). The latinist and the stylist both asked for *jumento*: the singular is one beast of burden, and in Brazil *jumento* is also what one calls a man without understanding — the sense of κτηνώδης after 72:21 *e não soube*. The row's *animais* stays for the plural herds (κτήνη).

options.label: um jumento
options.note: Ruling (v2); the Latin's beast of burden, and the Brazilian byword for a dull mind.

options.label: um animal
options.note: draft 1; the row's plural *animais* made singular; generic.

decisions.why: Verbless in the Latin and the Greek (καὶ ἐγὼ διὰ παντὸς μετὰ σοῦ): tense and mood are left open — 'and I am always with you', or 'and yet I [was] always with you', after the confession of 72:21–23. A copula would choose. Portuguese can say it verbless, and it is one of the lines people remember.

options.label: mas eu estou sempre convosco
options.note: the contrast and the tense supplied (MS1932 *mas sempre contigo*).

decisions.latin: et in voluntáte tua deduxísti me
decisions.why: *in voluntáte* instrumental: 'by your will' (the *volúntas* row: 29:8 *in voluntáte tua* → *pela vossa vontade*). *dedúcere me → guiar* (D22). The colon is a Gradual of Palm Sunday with 72:1–3 (Quad6-0, which reads *assumpsísti* for *suscepísti*).

D19 gives *suscípere* with a person *amparar*, made on ἀντιλαμβάνομαι (to take hold of, support). Here the Greek is προσελάβου, 'you took me to yourself', and the Palm Sunday Gradual reads *assumpsísti*: the sense is reception, not support. By D15's Greek test the verb follows the *suscípere (a thing)* row's *acolher* (6:10 προσδέχομαι), which MS1932 also has (*com glória me acolheste*).

decisions.latin: et a te quid vólui super terram?
decisions.why: *a te* (παρὰ σοῦ) is 'from you' — what did I want from you on earth — and was read by DRB and MS1932 as 'besides you' (*besides thee*, *fora de ti*). *de vós* holds both (from you / apart from you) as the Latin does; v2 drops the commas and puts it after the verb (stylist), as ordinary Portuguese orders it.

decisions.latin: Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in ætérnum
decisions.why: Two verbless members. The first (*Deus cordis mei*) is left as the Latin has it — heard as a cry or a vocative, which the Latin allows (MS1932 and DRB make it a vocative with a verb). In the second, *Deus* is the predicate of *pars mea* (the Greek has the article on *μερίς*, so 'my portion is God'); without a copula it would be heard as a second vocative. The copula is supplied there only (grammar, D2). The colon is a responsory (SanctiM Pent02-6b) and an Alleluia (06-04, 10-17), split at the mediant.

options.label: Deus é a minha parte
options.note: subject first; the Latin ends on *Deus*.

decisions.latin: qui elóngant se a te, períbunt
decisions.why: The *elongáre* row (open) keeps the Latin's *longe*: *pôr / ficar longe*. *se elóngant* reflexive → *se põem longe de vós*. MS1932 *se apartam*; the stylist refused *pôr longe* at 21:20 and asked *afastar*, which is *discédere*'s (the row keeps them apart).

decisions.latin: perdidísti omnes, qui fornicántur abs te
decisions.why: πορνεύοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ: to go whoring away from God, the prophets' image of idolatry. *se prostituem* says the image plainly; *fornicam* is the cognate but in Brazilian speech is coarse or a moral term for sex, not an image of unfaithfulness. MS1932 *os que te são infiéis* explains the image away (refused, rule 5). *abs te* → *longe de vós*, echoing *a te* in the first colon as the Latin does. *pérdere → fazer perecer* (D24; 72:27 is named there as keeping *períbunt: perdidísti* one figure). The colon is long (+4): *fizestes perecer* cannot be shortened without *perdestes*, which is heard as 'you lost'.

decisions.latin: Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est
decisions.why: The *adhærére* row (open) gives *apegar-se a* and names 72:28; the physical sense (*colar-se*, 21:16) is not this one. MS1932 *unir-me a Deus*. The versicle is known alone (Sancti 05-13, Urbis 07-17, Pent02-6b). *Mas para mim* answers 72:2 *Mas os meus pés* (*Mei autem … Mihi autem*), and *é bom* answers 72:1 *Deus é bom* — both kept.

*prædicátio* is both a proclaiming and a praising (L&S); the Greek is τὰς αἰνέσεις σου, 'your praises' (DRB *all thy praises*, MS1932 *todos os teus louvores*). *proclamar* is *prædicáre*'s verb, but *as vossas proclamações* is a decree's word. αἴνεσις is the Greek of *laus* (*sacrifícium laudis*), so by D15's test *louvores* may be shared; *laus* is not in this psalm.

choices.72:1: *Quam bonus* → *Como … é bom* (the *quam* row: *Como …!*). *his, qui recto sunt corde* → *para os que são retos de coração* (the *rectus corde* row, with the Latin's relative clause). Palm Sunday Tract (Quad6-0) and the Graduals of 02-27, 03-27, 06-04.
choices.72:2: *Mei autem* is fronted for contrast after 72:1; *Mas os meus pés* carries it without *quanto a mim*. The two colons keep the Latin's *pæne … pæne* (*quase … quase*).
choices.72:5: *labor → fadiga* (the row; 72:16 has the same noun). The final colon ends on a colon, as the Latin, since 72:6 draws the consequence (*Ídeo*).
choices.72:7: *prodíre → sair* (row, which names 72:7); *adeps → gordura* (row, which names 72:7: the concrete image kept; MS1932 glosses *coração sensual*). *quasi* → *como que*. The subject first, for the ear (D2).
choices.72:8: *cogitáre* shares its object with *loqui*; Portuguese says *pensar maldade* (content accusative, as 16:9b *falou soberba*), so the row's *em* is not used. *nequítia → maldade* (row, which names 72:8 beside *iniquitátem*). *locúti sunt* twice, *falaram* twice.
choices.72:9: *transívit in terra* → *passou pela terra* (διῆλθεν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς); *transíre → passar* as in 72:7.
choices.72:10: *dies pleni → dias cheios* (DRB *full days*, MS1932); *inveníri → ser achado*; *in eis → neles*.
choices.72:11: *scit … sciéntia* → *sabe … saber*: the root repeats as in the Latin (*sciéntia → o saber*, the row; *scire* is used absolutely, so *saber*, not the row's *conhecer*). 72:21 *nescívi* → *não soube* keeps the same verb.
choices.72:13: *Et dixi* → *E eu disse* (the pronoun so that *disse* is not heard as 'he said'). *sine causa → sem causa* (row). *et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas* copies 25:6 (*Lavarei as minhas mãos entre os inocentes*) as the Lavabo row asks.
choices.72:15: The first second-person pronoun of the psalm (*filiórum tuórum*): God, so *vossos*.
choices.72:17: *Sanctuárium → santuário* (kept apart from *sancta → o lugar santo*, as that row notes).
choices.72:19: *propter iniquitátem suam* → *por causa da sua iniquidade*, as 72:18 *propter dolos* → *por causa dos enganos*.
choices.72:20: *imágo → imagem*; *ad níhilum redígere → reduzir a nada* (row, which names 72:20 and 72:21: the same phrase twice in two verses, kept identical). *Dómine* → bare *Senhor*.
choices.72:21: *inflammáre → inflamar-se* (MS1932). *nescívi → não soube*, as 72:11. DO joins 72:21–22 in one prayed verse; 72:22 is not a separate id.
choices.72:24: The Gradual of Palm Sunday (Quad6-0) and of 03-27.
choices.72:26: *caro → carne*; *pars → parte* (row, kept apart from *pórtio → porção*); *in ætérnum → para sempre* (D23). The singular verb before two subjects (*Desfaleceu a minha carne e o meu coração*) is the Latin's and good Portuguese.
choices.72:27: *Quia ecce → Porque eis que* (*ecce → eis*, row).
choices.72:28: *spes → esperança*; the Latin's order (*pôr no Senhor Deus a minha esperança*) so that the colon ends on the hope. The whole of 72:28–28b is an Offertory (05-13) and a responsory (Bavaria 09-17).
choices.72:28b: *in portis* → *às portas* (MS1932): 'at the gates', where *nas portas* can be heard as 'on the doors'. *fília Sion → filha de Sião*.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm72.txt, 28 prayed verses (72:1–72:21, 72:23–72:28, 72:28b; DO joins biblical 72:21–22 in its 72:21); one mediant each, no flex. No titulus (D7). Liturgical uses (ps032/uses.py): 72:1 (+72:2–3) Graduals and the Palm Sunday Tract (Quad6-0); 72:24 Gradual (03-27; Quad6-0 with *assumpsísti*); 72:26 Alleluia (06-04, 10-17) and responsory (SanctiM Pent02-6b, *Deus cordis mei * et pars mea Deus in ætérnum*); 72:28–28b Offertory (05-13), versicles (Urbis 07-17, Bavaria 09-17, Pent02-6b).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps072.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932; no Diurnal: Ps 72 is a Matins psalm). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Rows applied, most of which name 72: *zeláre → invejar*, *prodíre → sair*, *adeps → gordura*, *nequítia → maldade*, *matutína → nas madrugadas*, *súbito → de repente*, *verúmtamen → todavia*, *ad níhilum redígere → reduzir a nada*, *renes → rins*, *juménta → animal*, *elongáre → pôr longe*, *pérdere → fazer perecer* (D24), *adhærére → apegar-se*, the Lavabo row (72:13), *tota die → o dia todo* (D24), *plaga → flagelo* (D39), *in ætérnum → para sempre* (D23), *dedúcere → guiar* (D22), *existimáre → pensar* (D44). Hard readings: 72:4 (*respéctus*, *firmaméntum*, D31 left to this psalm), 72:12 (verbless *Ecce, ipsi peccatóres*), 72:15 (indicative *reprobávi*), 72:18 (*posuísti* with no object), 72:26 (verbless). Two one-verb echoes kept on purpose: *ténuit / Tenuísti* (*tomar*) and *defecérunt / Defécit* (*desfalecer*).
